comparison: Both strongly support the correspondence between retinal and behavioral thresholds at backgrounds of 0.01-0.02 R*/rod/s (C1, C31, C37, C59). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative demonstration while peer reviewers explicitly praised this as a significant contribution. High agreement.

Both support localization to AII amacrine cells (C2, C57, C72). OpenEval cites spatial transfer and rod-cone separation experiments; peer reviewers affirmed the finding without methodological concerns. OpenEval includes C53 in its analysis while peer review explicitly mentions it. Strong agreement.

Both support single-photon sensitivity and rapid kinetics (C4, C5). OpenEval groups these with mean vs. variance control (C39, C67, C82) and modeling; peer review focuses on rapid kinetics (C42-C44, C68) and dimmest detectable backgrounds. Overlapping but differently organized support.

OpenEval supports mean-based control (C39, C67) as part of broader mechanism characterization; peer review separately affirms fluctuating background experiments (C40, C41) demonstrating mean vs. variance distinction. Both support but organize evidence differently.

Major disagreement on C20-C22 regarding excitatory vs. inhibitory contributions. OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 2 data; peer reviewers criticized presentation as 'particularly lacking in precise language' and marked evaluation as UNCERTAIN, requesting quantitative clarification.

Disagreement on Weber law behavior (C23-C25, C29). OpenEval finds excellent support from fits to Equation 1; peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN due to confusion about multiple gain measures and inconsistent definitions, requesting clarification on what was being measured.

Disagreement on noise suppression claims (C33, C34, C36). OpenEval finds support from Figures 3B and 3E with Poisson comparisons; peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, requesting clearer definitions of gain, noise, and background, and better explanation of how gain changes affect both signal and noise.

Both support rapid kinetics findings (C42-C44, C68). OpenEval emphasizes asymmetry between increases and decreases; peer review accepts rapid kinetics as part of systematic demonstration of adaptation at dimmest backgrounds. Strong agreement.

Both support spatial pooling requirements (C47, C52, C69). OpenEval combines Poisson modeling with spatial experiments; peer review explicitly affirms '1 or 2 photons absorbed within a collection of several hundred rods.' Strong agreement on convergence requirements.

Both support spatial transfer experiments (C48-C51) demonstrating hundreds of rods required. OpenEval details receptive field inference and rod density calculations; peer review affirms the overall finding without methodological concerns. Strong agreement.

Both support pathway-specific adaptation (C54-C56). OpenEval emphasizes lack of rod-to-cone transfer as critical constraint; peer review accepts finding (C54, C55, C70) without concerns. Strong agreement on pathway separation.

Both support inference about AII amacrine cells (C53). OpenEval notes logical inference from spatial pooling and convergence data; peer review explicitly mentions this in their affirmation statement. Agreement on localization logic.

Both support fluctuating background experiments (C40-C41) showing mean vs. variance control. OpenEval finds direct support from Figure 4; peer review accepts systematic experimental approach. Strong agreement on this specific result.

Both support comparison between retinal and behavioral measurements (C65-C66) and inference about post-retinal contributions. OpenEval notes reasonable inference; peer review accepts as part of successful integration of physiological and psychophysical data. Strong agreement.

Both support identification of multiple coordinated mechanisms (C76-C80). OpenEval synthesizes current and previous findings; peer review accepts integration of novel mechanism with known mechanisms. Strong agreement, though OpenEval notes C81 (evolutionary claim) is speculative.

OpenEval finds quantitative support for gain and threshold slope measurements (C32, C38) from Figures 3D and 3F. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific quantitative measurements.
OpenEval marks C26-C28 as UNCERTAIN due to unpublished mechanistic study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about background-dependent changes.

OpenEval finds support for noise comparisons to literature (C59-C61). While peer review mentions C59 in context of threshold correspondence (R1), no separate evaluation addresses the specific noise comparison claims.
OpenEval supports inference about ON cone bipolar cells (C73-C74) based on circuit architecture. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these cell-type specific predictions.
OpenEval supports modeling calculations (C86-C89) combining literature data with integration time measurements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific modeling results.
OpenEval notes C6-C8 provide established background context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are motivational rather than novel findings.
OpenEval notes C9-C19 provide established literature background and retinal circuitry context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval supports distinction of novel mechanism from previous work (C30, C71). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this distinction.
OpenEval supports literature context claims (C58, C62-C64). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual comparisons.
OpenEval marks C81 (evolutionary speculation) as UNCERTAIN while accepting C75 as established. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing evolutionary claims.
OpenEval notes C83-C85 are straightforward methodological statements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methods descriptions.
